name: Aurelia Retreat
desc: An imagined island retreat with editorial room discovery and a complete browser-local reservation simulation.
approach: Warm paper, olive tones and image-led compositions frame a calm arrival. The booking flow validates dates and guests, filters rooms by capacity and presents fictional itemized euro pricing before a clearly marked demo confirmation.
proof: Room discovery, date validation, capacity selection, price review, refresh persistence, cancellation and reset were verified in an isolated browser.
limit: A fictional property with illustrative licensed mood photography. No inventory service, payment or real reservation.

name: Kora Live
desc: A fictional cultural calendar that turns event discovery into an interactive seat-selection and demo-ticket journey.
approach: Original event artwork, a dark canvas and lively lime accents give each fictional gathering its own presence. Discovery filters lead into event details, selectable spots, transparent totals and a local ticket wallet.
proof: Selection rules reject duplicate, unavailable and invalid spots. Browser-local ticket persistence, repeat booking and reset flows were exercised.
limit: All events, venues, capacities and prices are fictional. Tickets are demo records, with no payment or real admission.

name: Fieldnote
desc: A working fictional studio dashboard connecting tasks, projects and people through board, list and calendar views.
approach: A restrained paper-and-moss interface gives space to day-to-day decisions. Task editing, creation and deletion update linked summaries; search and filters work across views, with a cancelable reset.
proof: Seed integrity tests passed. Task changes, view navigation, filtering, calendar movement and refresh persistence were tested locally.
limit: No real studio data, login, invitations, shared database or live integrations. Edits belong to the current browser.

name: Luma Academy
desc: A fictional learning academy with one complete visual-hierarchy course, an interactive poster lab and a progress dashboard.
approach: Warm editorial typography and original CSS artwork connect course discovery with practice. The working course includes lessons, a poster exercise, a three-question knowledge check and persistent learning progress.
proof: Course discovery, bookmarks, lessons, poster settings, quiz states, dashboard persistence and reset were exercised in isolated browser journeys.
limit: One course is complete; two others are upcoming previews. Achievements are samples and non-accredited. No real institution or enrollment service.

name: Naya Muse
desc: An original editorial store concept with photorealistic AI campaign imagery, product variants and a complete fictional bag-to-confirmation flow.
approach: The latest imagery comprises 20 original AI-generated campaign and product concepts. Product filtering, search, price sorting, clothing colours/sizes and cosmetic shades lead to a persistent multi-variant bag and acknowledged demo checkout.
proof: Variant, stock, storage and integer-price unit tests passed. Discovery, product details, bag changes, checkout and mobile layouts were verified.
limit: All products, people, prices and stock are fictional. Images do not document manufactured garments or tested cosmetics. No payment, personal-data collection or order submission.

name: Luma Galleria
desc: An original mall architecture study with an editable 3D model, matching 2D plan, actual model renders and an optional rotatable viewer.
approach: A 74 × 100 m concept footprint organizes 22 units around a glazed atrium and cross gallery. Limestone, bronze framing, timber fit-outs, transparent shopfronts, a gabled glass roof and a landscaped arrival plaza form a coherent model and plan.
proof: The exported GLB was loaded and its bounds, materials and roof meshes checked. Roof, shell and furniture toggles, view presets and the matching floor plan were exercised.
limit: A self-initiated architectural visualization, not a website project or certified construction package. Dimensions are chosen design values; structural, fire, accessibility and building-services engineering are not provided.
